novel_features.name: Order triage
novel_features.description: Splits the order queue into actionable buckets and flags payment gateways whose failure rate is climbing.
novel_features.rationale: Comparing today's failed-order rate against the trailing period requires stored history; a single API call only ever describes right now.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of listing orders by status when you need to know what is stuck and whether a gateway is degrading.

novel_features.name: Stock velocity and reorder list
novel_features.description: Units sold per day per variation divided into current stock, producing days-of-cover and a reorder list sorted by stockout date.
novel_features.rationale: No WooCommerce endpoint returns a demand denominator - product listings give stock with no sales velocity to divide it by.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to answer 'what do I reorder' - it is the one number the WooCommerce admin never shows.

novel_features.name: Revenue decomposition
novel_features.description: Breaks a revenue change between two periods into order-count, basket-size, per-product, refund, and coupon contributions.
novel_features.rationale: The Reports API returns totals for one period at a time and cannot decompose a delta into its causes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this over a sales report when the question is why a number moved, not what the number is.

novel_features.name: Refund rate by product
novel_features.description: Refunded units over sold units for every product and variation, so return-prone items surface by rate rather than raw count.
novel_features.rationale: Refunds and orders are separate endpoints and neither carries a per-product rate; the attribution needs a local line-item join.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to find margin leaks that a top-sellers report actively hides.

novel_features.name: Customer lifetime value and cohorts
novel_features.description: Per-customer lifetime value and order count, plus repeat-purchase retention bucketed by first-order month.
novel_features.rationale: Cohort retention and LTV are structurally absent from the Reports API and require grouping every synced order by customer.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the question is about customer quality over time rather than a single order.

novel_features.name: Catalog completeness audit
novel_features.description: Deterministic scan for publishable defects: missing images, empty descriptions, absent SKUs, zero prices, and unpriced or stockless variations.
novel_features.rationale: There is no defect endpoint - this is a rule engine over the synced product and variation tables, returning IDs rather than prose.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this before a campaign to catch broken listings while they are still cheap to fix.

novel_features.name: Public catalog snapshot
novel_features.description: Records a timestamped price, sale, and stock snapshot of any public WooCommerce store, with no credentials of any kind.
novel_features.rationale: The WooCommerce Store API is unauthenticated, so any store on the internet can be read - and prices arrive in minor units that must be normalized on write.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this on stores you do not own; every other WooCommerce tool assumes you hold admin keys.

novel_features.name: Catalog diff
novel_features.description: Compares two recorded snapshots to report added and delisted products, price moves with magnitude, sale windows, and stock flips.
novel_features.rationale: Pure local history - it issues no API call at read time, so it can answer questions about the past that the live API has already forgotten.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the payoff of catalog watch: what actually changed, rather than what is true right now.

narrative.headline: The only WooCommerce CLI with a local database - so it answers the compound questions the Reports API cannot, and reads any store on the internet without credentials.
narrative.value_prop: WooCommerce's REST API is complete but stateless: it tells you what is true right now, one question at a time. This CLI mirrors your store into local SQLite, which turns questions like stock velocity, refund rate by product, and cohort retention from spreadsheet chores into single commands. It also speaks the public Store API, so `catalog watch` and `catalog diff` work against competitor stores you have no keys for.
narrative.auth_narrative: WooCommerce has no central API host - every store serves its own at `https://<your-store>/wp-json/`. Point the CLI at yours with `WOOCOMMERCE_BASE_URL=https://your-store.com/wp-json`, then generate a key pair under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API and export `WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY` and `WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET`. Read scope is enough for every read command. The public catalog commands need no credentials at all and work against any store. Two host-level gotchas worth knowing: some servers strip the Authorization header (you will see a misleading "Consumer key is missing" error over HTTPS), and pretty permalinks must be enabled or `/wp-json/` returns 404 for everything.

quickstart.comment: confirm the CLI can see a store URL and credentials before anything hits the network
read a public catalog with no credentials at all - this works immediately
mirror your own store locally; every analysis command reads from here
the reorder list - units per day divided into current stock
what is stuck in the queue right now, and which gateway is failing

troubleshoots.symptom: 401 with "Consumer key is missing" even though credentials are set and the URL is HTTPS
troubleshoots.fix: The host is stripping the Authorization header. WooCommerce's documented workaround is passing credentials as query parameters - run `woocommerce-pp-cli doctor` to confirm the diagnosis.
Pretty permalinks are disabled. Enable them in Settings > Permalinks; the REST API has no routes without them.

troubleshoots.symptom: PUT or DELETE requests return 501 Method Not Implemented
troubleshoots.fix: ModSecurity is blocking the verb. Ask the host to allow REST verbs, or use the batch endpoints which POST instead.

troubleshoots.symptom: Prices from catalog commands look 100x too large
troubleshoots.fix: Store API prices are integer minor units. The CLI normalizes using each response's currency_minor_unit - if you are reading raw JSON yourself, divide accordingly.
They read the local mirror, not the API. Run `woocommerce-pp-cli sync --resources orders,products` first.

troubleshoots.symptom: A list command returns only 10 rows
troubleshoots.fix: That is WooCommerce's default per_page. Pass `--per-page 100` (the API maximum) or let `sync` paginate for you.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for WooCommerce store operations and analysis over the REST API: reading and mutating orders, products, variations, customers, coupons, taxes, shipping, and webhooks, and for the compound analytics that need history - stock velocity, refund rates, customer LTV, revenue decomposition. It is also the right tool for reading any public WooCommerce store's catalog without credentials, including competitor research and price tracking. Reach for it whenever a question spans more than one API call or more than one point in time.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for WordPress content (posts, pages, users, media) - it speaks only the WooCommerce namespaces; use the WordPress REST API or WP-CLI.

Do not use this CLI for server-side WooCommerce maintenance such as HPOS migration, database updates, attribute lookup table regeneration, or Blueprint import/export - those exist only in WP-CLI and require shell access to the WordPress host, with no REST equivalent.
Do not use this CLI to install or manage WooCommerce extensions or connect the store to WooCommerce.com - that is WP-CLI's `wc com` family.
Do not use this CLI to place real customer orders through the storefront checkout - the cart and checkout Store API routes are deliberately excluded.
Do not expect it to work against a WooCommerce store older than 3.5, which predates the wc/v3 namespace.

recipes.title: Find what to reorder before you stock out
recipes.explanation: Aggregates 30 days of order line items against current stock and returns only the four fields that drive a purchase order, keeping the response small enough to reason over directly.

recipes.title: Track a competitor's prices without any credentials
recipes.command: woocommerce-pp-cli catalog watch --store https://woocommerce.com --max-pages 2 && woocommerce-pp-cli catalog diff --store https://woocommerce.com --since 30d
recipes.explanation: The first command records a snapshot through the public Store API; the second compares it against earlier snapshots to surface price moves, new products, and delistings.

recipes.title: Explain a bad week
recipes.explanation: Decomposes the revenue delta into order count, average basket, per-product contribution, refunds, and coupon discount, so the cause is a row rather than a hunch.

recipes.title: Audit a catalog before a campaign
recipes.explanation: Returns each defect rule with a count and the offending product IDs, which is directly actionable without opening the admin UI.

recipes.title: Pull deeply nested order data without drowning in it
recipes.explanation: Order payloads are large and deeply nested; dotted --select paths narrow them to the handful of fields an agent actually needs.
